budget_semantics: the shared token budget is an admission limit used by the guard, not an observed ceiling; the HIGH scenario assumes a run consumes exactly that much and is a model, not a measurement
child_pricing_rule: child prompt tokens are billed at the cache-miss rate because the provider reports no child cache split; they are counted once and never reported as misses

value_types.provider_reported_usage: prompt/completion tokens and the main cache split, as the provider reported them
value_types.budget_admission_estimate: the shared 500000-token guard limit: an admission threshold the runtime enforces, not a measured ceiling and not a bill
value_types.pricing_estimate: USD derived from the frozen per-million snapshot in experiments/configs/eval-benchmark.yaml
value_types.actual_billing: UNKNOWN: the provider exposes no per-run invoice

wall_clock.note: the pilots measured the model loop only; sandbox provisioning and export add to it

pricing.basis: frozen config; the file itself labels it an upper bound for deepseek-chat

assumptions: one run costs about what one prompt pilot cost; the tasks are comparable, not equal
the HIGH scenario assumes a run consumes its whole 500000-token admission budget
cache behaviour is held at the observed mixture; a cold cache raises the miss share
child prompt tokens are priced as misses because no child cache split is reported
the price is the frozen snapshot, not a live quote
